Camera Discovery and Connection

This page describes the camera search, continuous discovery and connection confirmation.

Camera Address Format

Online APIs that access a camera generally use the camera address as the first ip parameter, for example:

127.0.0.1:5000
10.10.11.35:5000

Search for Cameras

Search result

SearchCamera(), search_camera(), and searchCamera() search the current network and return the cameras found in that search.

The search may take several seconds.

Each result includes the camera address, serial number, model, and alias.

Python

import epiceye

cameras = epiceye.search_camera()
if not cameras:
    raise SystemExit("No camera was searched")

ip = cameras[0]["ip"]
print("Use camera:", ip)

C++

#include "epiceye.h"
using namespace TFTech;

std::vector<EpicEyeInfo> cameras;
if (EpicEye::searchCamera(cameras) && !cameras.empty()) {
    std::string ip = cameras[0].IP;
}

C#

using TFTech;

var cameras = EpicEye.SearchCamera();
string ip = cameras[0].IP;
Can’t find the camera?

  1. Confirming that computers are in the same section as cameras;

  2. Check if the firewall’s stopped. UDP Broadcasting (discovery of reliance on broadcasting);

  3. Known IP Use it directly. ip, Skip the search.

Continuous Discovery

Continuous discovery maintains an up-to-date camera list while the application is running:

  • C#: subscribe to DiscoveredCamerasChanged, start or stop discovery with StartDiscovery() / StopDiscovery(), and read the list with GetDiscoveredCameras().

  • C++: register a callback with setDiscoveryCallback(), start or stop discovery with startDiscovery() / stopDiscovery(), and read the list with getDiscoveredCameras().

  • Python: register a callback with set_discovery_callback(), start or stop discovery with start_discovery() / stop_discovery(), and read the list with get_discovered_cameras().

When the event or callback runs, call the corresponding list method to read the latest camera list.

Python

import epiceye

def on_changed() -> None:
    print(epiceye.get_discovered_cameras())

epiceye.set_discovery_callback(on_changed)
epiceye.start_discovery()
# Apply exit:epiceye.stop_discovery()

C++

EpicEye::setDiscoveryCallback([] {
    std::vector<EpicEyeInfo> cameras;
    EpicEye::getDiscoveredCameras(cameras);
});
EpicEye::startDiscovery();
// Apply exit:EpicEye::stopDiscovery();

C#

EpicEye.DiscoveredCamerasChanged += () =>
    Console.WriteLine(EpicEye.GetDiscoveredCameras().Count);
EpicEye.StartDiscovery();
// Apply exit:EpicEye.StopDiscovery();
Continuous detection of life cycle

Register the event or callback before starting discovery. Read the current list when needed, and stop discovery before the application exits.

Use a Known Address

When the camera address is known, pass it directly as ip; camera discovery is not required.

Confirm Connection

Read basic information to confirm the camera address and service connection.

Python

info = epiceye.get_info("127.0.0.1:5000")
print(info)   # None Could not close temporary folder: %s

C++

EpicEyeInfo info;
if (!EpicEye::getInfo("127.0.0.1:5000", info)) {
    // Connection failed
}

C#

var info = EpicEye.GetInfo("127.0.0.1:5000");
Console.WriteLine(info.Data?.SN);
